results.text:
Nebius GPU Cloud Review 2026: Prices and Terms | C9 Group

By Kristijan Sekereš

# Nebius in 2026: a GPU cloud review for teams leaving AWS or Azure

Nebius is the AI cloud of Nebius Group N.V., a Dutch company whose shares trade on Nasdaq and which was called Yandex N.V. until August 2024. It is a GPU cloud first. A new account can start up to 32 H100 GPUs in Finland, or 32 B300s in France or the UK, after a USD 25 card charge and without a sales call, and the H100 costs USD 4.50 (EUR 4.01) an hour, 39% less than AWS's nearest H100 in Stockholm. Managed Slurm and Kubernetes come with it, and traffic out of VMs is free. The catch is in the terms: GPU prices rose twice in 2026, by about half in four months, on a few days' notice; regions are single sites with no availability zones documented; and the general-purpose catalogue is too thin to replace an AWS estate.

This article is one of a series comparing 24 European cloud providers with AWS and Azure; the overview puts them side by side. Everything below was checked on 15 and 16 October 2026 against Nebius's documentation, legal terms, price pages, status page and postmortems, its SEC filings and user reports, each at its source. We did not open an account or run workloads.

## At a glance

| | Nebius |
| --- | --- |
| Headquarters and control | Amsterdam (registered office at Schiphol). Nebius Group N.V., Class A shares on Nasdaq. A trust of the founder and CEO Arkady Volozh's family holds 51.62% of the votes for about 11% of the equity, which makes Nebius a Nasdaq "Controlled Company" |
| Regions and zones | In the EU: Finland (eu-north1), France (eu-west1, eu-west2) and Madrid (eu-south1). Also two UK regions, one in Israel and two in the US. No availability zones documented |
| GPUs | Per GPU-hour, with the preset's vCPUs and RAM: H100 USD 4.50 (EUR 4.01, Finland only), H200 USD 5.40 (EUR 4.82), B300 USD 9.50 (EUR 8.48). B200 only outside the EU |
| Workload A (starter) | USD 52.39 (EUR 46.74) a month in eu-west1, France |
| Workload B (production) | USD 546.43 (EUR 487.54) with a two-host database. No load balancer for plain VMs, only inside Managed Kubernetes. The database SLA needs three hosts: USD 655.24 |
| Egress | Free from VMs, and public IPs are free. Object Storage Standard: USD 0.015 per GiB |
| Compute SLA | 99.5% per VM, GPU VMs included. Credits capped at 30%, claimed within 14 days of the month's end |
| Included support | Free tickets for every account; first response within 30 minutes for a critical ticket |
| Who can sign up | Anyone with a Google, GitHub or Microsoft login and a card. Activation follows a USD 25 charge credited to the balance; no identity document step is described |

## What you can build

Nebius sells GPUs, the tools to train and serve models on them, and a small general-purpose layer. Status is general availability unless noted; preview services "come without guaranteed service levels".

| What you need | Nebius | AWS | Azure |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CPU virtual machines | AMD EPYC Genoa in every region, Intel Ice Lake in Finland; 2 to 256 vCPU at a fixed 1:4 ratio of vCPU to RAM | EC2 | Virtual Machines |
| GPU virtual machines | H100, H200, B200, B300 (1 or 8 per VM); RTX PRO 6000, L40S | EC2 P and G families | NC and ND series |
| GPU clusters | InfiniBand: 400 Gbps (8 x ConnectX-7) on H100, H200 and B200, 800 Gbps (8 x ConnectX-8) on B300; GB200 and GB300 NVL72 racks through sales | EC2 UltraClusters, SageMaker HyperPod | ND series with InfiniBand |
| Slurm | Managed Soperator, Nebius's open-source Kubernetes operator for Slurm (Apache-2.0), in eight regions | ParallelCluster, HyperPod | CycleCloud Slurm |
| Kubernetes | Managed Kubernetes, CNCF certified for v1.36; free control plane with three etcd replicas | EKS | AKS |
| Storage | Network SSD disks, shared filesystem, WEKA; S3-compatible Object Storage in three classes | EBS, EFS, FSx for Lustre, S3 | Managed Disks, Azure Files, Managed Lustre, Blob Storage |
| Relational database | Managed PostgreSQL, version 16 only, in six regions | RDS | Azure Database for PostgreSQL |
| Model inference | Token Factory (formerly AI Studio): an OpenAI-compatible API for open-weight models, dedicated endpoints, fine-tuning; Serverless AI for your own containers; Managed MLflow | Bedrock, SageMaker | Azure AI Foundry, Azure ML |
| Networking | VPC, Cloud Interconnect; a load balancer only as a Kubernetes service | VPC, Direct Connect, ELB | VNet, ExpressRoute, Load Balancer |
| Security and operations | IAM with SAML single sign-on, KMS; SecretStash, Monitoring, Logging and Audit Logs in preview | IAM, KMS, CloudWatch, CloudTrail | Entra ID, Key Vault, Azure Monitor |

Missing outright: bare metal, managed MySQL, Redis or Valkey, MongoDB, Kafka and OpenSearch, functions, queues and pub/sub, a standalone load balancer, a CDN, documented DDoS protection, a general backup service and availability zones. Object Storage has no Object Lock, replication rules or event notifications. Managed PostgreSQL is not offered in Madrid. Token Factory changes quickly: Nebius removed two batches of serverless model IDs, on 22 June and 31 August 2026, with no automatic rerouting.

The tooling covers a gRPC and REST API, SDKs for Go, Python and TypeScript, a CLI and a Terraform provider, still pre-1.0 (0.6.71, published 15 October 2026) and not found on the OpenTofu registry.

## What it costs

Nebius list prices in US dollars, the only billing currency outside Israel, VAT excluded, checked 15 and 16 October 2026. Euros are at the ECB rate of 15 October (1 EUR = 1.1208 USD).

### GPUs

GPU VMs are billed per second. On the H100, H200, B200, B300 and RTX PRO 6000 the GPU-hour price includes the preset's vCPUs and RAM (16 vCPUs and 200 GB per H100); disks are extra.

| GPU | Regions | USD per GPU-hour | EUR | Default quota |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 80 GB | eu-north1 (Finland) only | 4.50 | 4.01 | 32 |
| H200 141 GB | eu-north1, eu-west1 (France), us-central1 | 5.40 | 4.82 | 32 in Finland, 8 in France, 0 in us-central1 |
| B200 | us-central1, me-west1 (Israel) | 8.50 | 7.58 | 0 |
| B300 | eu-west2 (France), uk-south1, us-north1 | 9.50 | 8.48 | 32 in each |
| RTX PRO 6000 96 GB | eu-south1 (Madrid), uk-south2, us-central1 | 1.80 | 1.61 | 32, except 0 in us-central1 |
| L40S 48 GB | eu-north1 | from 1.55 | 1.38 | 32 |
| GB200, GB300 NVL72 | not listed per region | "Contact us" | | sales |

AWS sells no H100, H200 or B200 in Frankfurt. Its nearest H100 costs USD 7.36 (EUR 6.57) per GPU-hour in Stockholm, where the H200 is USD 8.47 and the B200 USD 17.91; its B300 is USD 27.19 in London. Azure charges USD 15.98 per GPU-hour on its 8-GPU InfiniBand H100 size, which it does not sell in Frankfurt, and USD 13.78 for the H200 in Frankfurt. Nebius's H100 costs 61% of AWS's Stockholm price and its B300 35% of AWS's London price. AWS starts every account at zero GPU quota.

A quota is not capacity. For on-demand and preemptible services the Services Agreement lets Nebius "refuse to provide the Services at its sole discretion based on available capacity, price, cluster utilization or other operational considerations".

Preemptible and committed. Since 8 October 2026 spot prices move: "from" USD 0.99 per GPU-hour on B300 and B200 and USD 0.79 on H200, H100 and RTX PRO 6000, changing "as often as every 15 minutes", up to "one cent below the current pay-as-you-go (PAYG) on-demand rate". Commitments promise "up to 35% less than on-demand rates" for multi-month cluster reservations, for companies only, through sales, with no public price list. Rack-scale systems are sold that way too, and their fee covers the whole rack, including a "Maintenance Buffer" of 2 of its 18 nodes.

Price changes. On-demand GPU prices rose on 1 June and again on 1 October 2026, in USD per GPU-hour:

| GPU | Until 31 May 2026 | From 1 June | From 1 October | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 | 2.95 | 3.85 | 4.50 | +52.5% |
| H200 | 3.50 | 4.50 |
